edits.old: You know that you will spend m wrong tries to perform the combo and during the i-th try you will make a mistake right after p_i-th button (1 ≤ p_i < n) (i.e. you will press first p_i buttons right and start performing the combo from the beginning). It is guaranteed that during the m+1-th try you press all buttons right and finally perform the combo.
edits.new: You make m failed practice attempts. During the i-th attempt you press the last p_i buttons of s, in their original left-to-right order, where 1 ≤ p_i < n. After these failed attempts you make one successful attempt pressing all n buttons in order.

edits.old: I.e. if s="abca", m=2 and p = [1, 3] then the sequence of pressed buttons will be 'a' (here you're making a mistake and start performing the combo from the beginning), 'a', 'b', 'c', (here you're making a mistake and start performing the combo from the beginning), 'a' (note that at this point you will not perform the combo because of the mistake), 'b', 'c', 'a'.
edits.new: For example, if s="abca", m=2 and p=[1,3], the attempts press "a", then "bca", then the successful full string "abca".

edits.old: the number of characters pressed right during the i-th try
edits.new: the number of suffix characters pressed during the i-th failed attempt

edits.old: It is guaranteed that the answer for each letter does not exceed 2 ⋅ 10^9.
edits.new: The input retains this guarantee: if the failed attempts used the first p_i characters instead, followed by the full string, each letter would be pressed at most 2 ⋅ 10^9 times. The requested suffix-based counts must be printed exactly and may exceed that value.
